disagreement_structure.what_that_says: THE POSITIVE QUESTION WAS NEARLY SETTLED AND THE NEGATIVE ONE WAS NOT. 'Is there an ablation arm' produced ONE contradiction in 130. 'Is there an arm that is NOT an ablation' produced 24, plus 37 refusals from one seat and 0 from the other. Identifying what something IS is a different order of task from identifying what it IS NOT.

the_question_itself_was_wrong: 20 of the 25 are trials of something done AROUND an ablation that every arm receives. Asked 'does any arm deliver catheter ablation', the honest answer for those is YES -- which is exactly what makes the ablation BACKGROUND rather than the intervention. THIS PROJECT ALREADY LEARNED THIS: topic_identity.locate() was reframed from 'where does the drug appear' to 'WHAT EXACTLY WAS RANDOMISED' and two defects dissolved under it. The adjudication packet reintroduced the discarded form. The 47.7% agreement is substantially a measurement of that ambiguity rather than of the trials, and the seats were answering two different readings of a question that had two.
consequence_for_the_remaining_45: The 43 SOFT disagreements and 2 both-UNCLEAR are NOT hand-read here. Given that the question was ambiguous, hand-reading answers to it would inherit the ambiguity. They are to be RE-ASKED with the corrected question -- what differs between the arms -- which is a re-run, not a backlog of readings. Recorded as outstanding rather than resolved.

trials.why: catheter ablation vs EXTERNAL ELECTRIC CARDIOVERSION. The control is another procedure, not medical therapy. codex B=NO was right.
four arms, two ablation technologies plus a loop recorder and a pacemaker. No medical arm. codex B=NO right.
percutaneous LAA closure vs catheter ablation -- two interventional strategies against each other. codex B=NO right.
CABG/AVR plus SURGICAL pulmonary vein isolation vs CABG/AVR alone. Surgical PVI during cardiac surgery is not catheter ablation. BOTH seats said A=NO and were right.
CAVOTRICUSPID ISTHMUS ablation -- the flutter line in the right atrium -- not pulmonary vein isolation for atrial fibrillation.
CABG plus surgical PVI vs isolated CABG. Surgical again.
'surgical prevention of atrial fibrillation' during rheumatic valve surgery.
MENTAL TRAINING vs no intervention, in patients who have all had an ablation. The ablation is the setting; the contrast is a behavioural programme.
ROTATIONAL ANGIOGRAPHY vs none, during cryoballoon ablation. The contrast is an imaging technique.
LAA closure vs radiofrequency ablation vs both. Three interventional arms, no medical one.
the same three-arm design as NCT04376606.
2-HOBA vs placebo to prevent early recurrence AFTER ablation. The randomised contrast is a drug and the ablation is background.

OESOPHAGEAL COOLING DEVICE vs a temperature probe DURING AF ablation. THE ONLY LIMB-A CONTRADICTION IN 130: codex read `Device: ensoETM. Esophageal cooling during AF ablation` as an ablation arm because the string contains 'AF ablation'. agy read the contrast correctly. A substring inside a device description, which is precisely the matching-placebo trap in another costume.

Sentinel CEREBRAL PROTECTION DEVICE during ablation vs standard of care.

HAEMOSTASIS technique and bed-rest duration after venous access for ablation.

two TRANSSEPTAL PUNCTURE strategies.
